chunks: And he also narrated - Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Abd al-Malik from Sulayman ibn Khalid who said:

I asked him about a man who trod on the egg of a sandgrouse and broke it. He said: 'He sends a male ram for each egg from the sheep, just as he sends a male ram for each egg from the camels. And whoever hits an egg, upon him is a young sheep from the sheep.'

His saying (peace be upon him): 'And whoever hits an egg, upon him is a young sheep from the sheep,' does not contradict the earlier reports, because a young sheep is only obligatory upon him specifically when there is a chick in the egg, as we said regarding the ostrich egg: a she-camel is only obligatory upon him when there are chicks in it. And that which indicates that its ruling is the ruling of the ostrich egg is what he narrated:

key_terms.الْبَدَنَةُ: A young she-camel (specifically used as compensation)
key_terms.مَخَاضٌ: A young sheep (specifically used as compensation)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for accidentally breaking an egg while performing Hajj?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies the apparent discrepancy between earlier reports by distinguishing between eggs containing a formed fetus and those that do not, applying the specific compensation of a 'makhadh' (young sheep) only when a fetus is present. This ruling draws a direct parallel to the compensation for ostrich eggs, demonstrating the juristic principle of analogical extension (qiyas) within the category of accidental Ihram violations.
